summary: Four tickets, all built. I could not break tenant isolation, the rank floors, the op-key idempotency or the answer table's RLS, and the ledger held under a two-connection race. Twelve defects survived verification. The two that matter most are behavioural: (1) a completeness witness that only ONE reading channel finds now blocks a payroll summary that prints a complete, agreed run-totals row -- a page that posted unattended before 0343 -- driven and proved on clara_l07; (2) clara.answer_payroll_completeness posts through the unattended poster with no maker-checker and no high-stakes arm at all, so one bookkeeper's click books an entry clara.is_high_stakes() calls high-stakes, which the sibling settlement door in 0298 would have left a draft for a distinct checker. Beside them: #1059's reverse ceremony is two transactions with no compensation and no retry path; every posted payroll entry now mislabels its own state_version; the registry basis #1061 republished is contradicted by #1048 in the same lane; and the person answering the parked question is never told that the entry their yes books omits the employer's own statutory cost.
verified_sound: Tenant isolation on clara.answer_payroll_completeness: firm B's owner on firm A's parked document is refused CLR11 'payroll summary not found', byte-identical to the refusal for a document id that does not exist -- no existence oracle.
Rank floor: a viewer is refused CLR04 'insufficient role'; a member whose firm_memberships row is 'removed' is refused CLR04 'actor has no active membership'; clara_agent_ro has no EXECUTE (42501).

Idempotency: the same op_key with a flipped answer is refused CLR10 'op_key reused with different args'; the same op_key with the same payload replays the cached receipt and writes no second answer row.
Race, two real connections, both answering yes: one posts, the other is refused; exactly ONE journal entry and ONE answer row afterwards. The ledger belt holds (the refusal's shape is ADV-07).
RLS: clara.payroll_completeness_answers is clara_authenticated SELECT under firm_id = clara.jwt_firm(), revoked from clara_agent_ro, with append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE triggers.

Integer cents: the row identity gross-(epf+socso+eis+pcb)=net holds exactly over the summed columns; a mixed page (employer contributions printed, gross/net summed) still balances -- driven, 11 legs, Dr 576145 = Cr 576145.
Asia/Kuala_Lumpur calendar day: posting_date is the last day of the payslip's own month (2026-07-31 for a July run), never today's date.

Splice anchors: both SectionD and SectionJ count their anchor, require exactly one occurrence, refuse a no-op, and re-read the COMMITTED catalog in both the first-apply and redo branches; SectionJ's postcheck pins all sixteen pre-existing row-kind markers, the seventeenth once and the split predicate twice.
apps/web/tests/firm-scope-db-pins.corpus.ts carries an entry for 0343 whose sha256 (97acf5a3771005fd440a9da25a8de0c04a8de4cb365b4b929d4d114373b7873f) matches the file on disk byte for byte.

Gates I re-ran myself: the five payroll/registry batteries with the full $GATES chain -> 99 tests, 99 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; eight focused apps/web files -> 94 tests, 94 pass, 0 fail; node scripts/check-frozen-evaluators.mjs -> OK, 12 evaluators.

findings.title: A completeness witness only ONE channel finds blocks a payroll summary that prints a complete run-totals row
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:1516-1523 (the verdict folds any witness state='channels_disagree' into the channels_agree rung) and :571-573 (the evaluator calls a value-vs-not_printed split 'channels_disagree')
findings.evidence: Driven on clara_l07 through the real lane (payrollDoc -> router -> claimTask -> clara.persist_payroll_facts). CONTROL, a fully printed #946 page with no witness asked at all: posted=true, no rung. PROBE, the SAME fully printed page where the text channel answers payroll.run.employee_count='2' and the vision channel answers not_printed: posted=false, rung='channels_agree', reason='channels_disagree', detail.fields=['payroll.run.employee_count'], entries written = 0. Sentence shown to the person: 'Payroll run February 2026 was not posted: the two readings of this payslip disagree (payroll.run.employee_count). Check the page and re-file it.' The evaluator's own witness object for that case reads {state: channels_disagree, reason: one_channel_read_a_witness_the_other_did_not}.
findings.why_it_matters: The witness exists as a FALLBACK for a page that prints no totals. Here it vetoes a page that prints all eleven totals, that both channels agree on, and whose arithmetic holds -- a page the lane has posted unattended since #946. The refusal is also unactionable: the page is fine, and 're-file it' re-runs the same two models. The likely production split is not two models reading different NUMBERS (which the arm was written for) but one model spotting a small 'Total employees:' label the other misses -- exactly the value-vs-not_printed case. It is latent today only because the frozen payrollFacts_v1 prompts do not ask the two questions; the ticket's own successor contract (report section 9.1) tells the next lane to add exactly those two optional prompts, which arms it.
findings.required_fix: Fold a witness channels_disagree into the channels_agree rung only when the witness is load-bearing -- i.e. only when the plan actually needs a row sum (v_needs_sum). Failing that, treat a value-vs-not_printed split as 'absent' (which parks the question) and keep 'channels_disagree' for two channels that read two different COUNTS, which is the case the comment at 0343:1516-1520 argues for. Add a cell that drives a fully printed page with a one-sided witness and asserts it still posts.

findings.title: answer_payroll_completeness books a high-stakes entry with no checker, through the unattended poster
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:2340-2342 (the yes arm calls clara._post_payroll_run) and :1910 (the poster self-approves: status='approved', checker_actor = clara.agent_user_id())
findings.evidence: Driven on clara_l07. Set the firm's high_stakes_amount_cents to 100 (RM 1.00); parked a run whose gross sum is 500000 cents; a bookkeeper answered yes through clara.answer_payroll_completeness. Receipt: posted=true, entry_id set. The row: status='approved', checker_actor = maker_actor (both clara.agent_user_id()), last_human_editor = NULL. clara.is_high_stakes(<that entry>) returns TRUE. The estate's own answer to this situation is one migration earlier: packages/db/migrations/0298_payroll_net_pay_settlement.sql:494 -- 'if clara.is_high_stakes(v_entry) then ... LEAVE IT A DRAFT and let the ordinary approve door finish it' -- and payroll-settlement.test.mjs S7 pins it for the settlement of the SAME run's net pay for the SAME amount.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the first human-initiated post the payroll family has ever had, and it is the one case where a second pair of eyes matters most: the figure is not on the page. One bookkeeper's single click approves an unlimited-value payroll entry that no checker sees, and the ledger records the AGENT as both maker and checker while the human who authorised it appears only inside flags->payroll_run->posting_basis->answer. The estate is now inconsistent with itself: settling the payment is high-stakes-gated, posting the run on a computed figure is not.
findings.required_fix: Consult clara.is_high_stakes on the entry the answer would post and take 0298's own posture: leave it a draft for clara.approve_entry, say so in the receipt (the awaiting_checker shape 0298 already returns), and keep the Needs-you row until a checker finishes it. Separately, set last_human_editor (or the equivalent attribution the estate uses) to the answering actor on an answer-driven post, so the ledger names the human on its face.

findings.title: The reverse ceremony is two transactions with no compensation, and a partial failure locks the panel's only path shut forever
findings.where: apps/web/components/bank/payroll-settlements-section.tsx, confirmReverse: await unmatchBankMatch(...) then await reverseEntry(...) inside one part.act -- two separate door calls and therefore two separate transactions
findings.evidence: Driven inside a transaction I rolled back on clara_l07: a second clara.unmatch_bank_match on an already-unmatched match is refused CLR10, detail {"reason":"already_unmatched","match_id":...} -- the live body of clara._unmatch_bank_match_core (read with pg_get_functiondef on the lane database) raises it at its status guard. clara._payroll_net_pay_unsettled's live body reads ONLY the 2040 ledger legs (credits from payroll_run entries, debits from anything not payroll_obligation and not a reversal mirror) and never looks at clara.bank_matches. And confirmReverse's success callback -- which is what removes the card from justSettled -- only runs on success.
findings.why_it_matters: If unmatch lands and reverse_entry then refuses (a closed period, a CLR31 opening-boundary preflight, a concurrent reversal), the estate is left with (a) a settlement entry still approved, so the run still reads FULLY SETTLED by the ledger and stays hidden from get_payroll_settlement_candidates, and (b) the bank line freed and offerable to any other entry -- so the same payment can be matched twice. The panel's card is still there with a Reverse button, and pressing it can never succeed again, because step one now always refuses already_unmatched. The person's only way out is the Journals workbench. The lane's report records this as follow-up 10.4 ('a confusing SECOND refusal'); it is not confusing, it is a dead end over an inconsistent ledger.
findings.required_fix: Either make the retry resume from where it stopped (treat already_unmatched as success for this composition), or do what the report itself named and did not build: one server-side composite door (clara.reverse_payroll_settlement) that runs both steps in ONE transaction under one op_key. Whichever, add a cell that scripts unmatch-succeeds-then-reverse-refuses and asserts the panel still offers a path that works.

findings.title: Every posted payroll entry records state_version 'v1' while the reading it came from is banked as v2
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:1866 -- 'state_version', coalesce(v->'plan'->>'plan_version','v1') -- inside the v_flags object this file deliberately widened with posting_basis (0297:964 carried over verbatim)
findings.evidence: Live join on clara_l07 over the six most recent row_sum posts: in every one, document_extractions.envelope->'payroll_state'->>'state_version' = 'v2' while journal_entries.flags->'payroll_run'->>'state_version' = 'v1'. The flag is read off the PLAN's plan_version literal ('plan_version','v1' at 0343:1229), which is not the state's version and never was.
findings.why_it_matters: 0343's stated premise is that 'an auditor reading the LEDGER must be able to tell a figure the document states from one this estate computed' (its own comment at :1862). The entry now says the figures came from evaluator v1, which cannot produce a completeness verdict at all. Before 0343 there was only one state version, so the literal was accidentally right; 0343 mints a second one and makes the flag systematically wrong for every entry the lane posts from here on, including the ones sitting in clara_l07 now.
findings.required_fix: Populate the flag from the state that was judged, not from the plan version -- the verdict already carries it. If the flag is meant to be the plan's version, rename the key (it is written at the draft insert and clara._tf_entry_immutable freezes flags afterwards, so a rename is a migration, not an edit) and add a separate key for the evaluator version.

findings.kind: published claim contradicted by the same lane
findings.title: The registry basis #1061 published is wrong in two ways once #1048 lands beside it
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0342_payroll_registry_business_operation_supported.sql (the basis sentence it installs), live on clara_l07 at registry_version 7; 0343's tail explicitly asserts clara.document_capabilities was NOT republished
findings.evidence: The live basis for payroll_summary/application/pdf reads: 'Where both reading channels agree, every arithmetic check passes, every account resolves in this client's own chart, the run's own month is established and no payroll entry for that client and month is already posted, the run posts unattended: gross pay and the employer's own EPF, SOCSO, EIS and HRDF cost are debited, and EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF payable plus salaries payable are credited for the net.' (a) A page satisfying all five listed conditions that prints no run totals and witnesses nothing does NOT post unattended -- I drove exactly that and got rung='completeness_witness', reason='completeness_unwitnessed', completeness.parked=true and a Needs-you question a named person must answer. (b) The entry a witnessed row sum posts has SIX legs -- Dr 6000 500000; Cr 2100 55000, Cr 2110 2450, Cr 2120 980, Cr 2130 16000, Cr 2040 425570 -- with no employer EPF/SOCSO/EIS debit and no HRDF leg on either side (driven).
findings.why_it_matters: clara.document_capabilities is the estate's PUBLISHED statement of what it does with a document kind; #1061 rewrote it as an exhaustive 'Where X, Y, Z ... the run posts unattended' and raised the registry version to say so. Within the same lane, #1048 added a sixth condition and a new human act and left the sentence standing, and its tail actively asserts the registry was not republished. The leg list was already an overstatement of 0297's 'an unprinted line produces no leg' rule; 0343 makes it structurally false for a whole new class of post, because the per-employee row vocabulary has no employer columns to sum.
findings.required_fix: Republish the payroll_summary rows in a new migration (registry_version 8) with a basis that names the completeness witness, the parked question, and the fact that a row-sum entry books gross, the four employee deductions and the net and nothing else. An applied migration is immutable, so this is 0343's successor's work, not an edit to 0342.

findings.title: The person answering the parked question is not told the entry their yes books omits the employer's own statutory cost
findings.evidence: The sentence a person reads, driven on clara_l07: 'This payroll summary for October 2026 prints no total; is this every employee for the month? Clara read 2 employee line(s), totalling RM 5,000.00 gross and RM 4,255.70 net. Answer yes and the run posts from those lines; answer no and it stays unposted.' The web confirm copy adds only 'Clara will post this payroll run from the employee lines it read, and record your answer as the basis.' The entry that yes actually books (driven) carries six legs and plan.unprinted = ['payroll.run.epf_employer','payroll.run.socso_employer','payroll.run.eis_employer','payroll.run.hrdf_levy'] -- the employer's EPF, SOCSO and EIS cost and the HRDF levy are accrued NOWHERE, on either side.
findings.why_it_matters: The standing owner ruling is that Clara asks for a professional judgement; a professional judgement given without the material consequence is not one. The migration header names this residual honestly (:73-89) and the README repeats it, but neither is on the screen where the click happens. A bookkeeper answering yes reasonably believes the month's payroll is booked; the employer-side cost and the HRDF levy are silently left to be found later, and in Malaysia those are remitted against a filed return. The question asked ('is this every employee?') is also not the question whose answer the entry's completeness depends on.
findings.required_fix: Put the residual in the sentence the verdict builds (it already has plan.unprinted in hand) or in the confirm copy: name the accounts that will get no leg and say they must be booked another way. Cheapest honest version: append 'The page prints no employer EPF, SOCSO, EIS or HRDF figure, so those are not booked by this entry.' whenever plan.unprinted is non-empty.

findings.title: Two people answering the same question at the same moment get a raw SQLSTATE 23505, not a named refusal
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:2325-2329 (the insert) against the UNIQUE on extraction_id at :1296
findings.evidence: Two real connections on clara_l07, both clara_authenticated, both answering yes on the same parked document with different op keys. The first returns posted=true with an entry id. The second: error 23505, 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "payroll_completeness_answers_extraction_id_key"'. Afterwards: exactly one journal entry and exactly one answer row, so the belt itself works. apps/web/lib/firm/payroll-completeness.ts names three refusals it can surface (no_parked_completeness_question, payroll_completeness_answer_invalid, not_filed); 23505 is none of them and carries no detail.reason a refusal mapper can read.
findings.why_it_matters: The overlap window is not small -- it spans clara._post_payroll_run, which drafts, validates and approves a journal entry. Two bookkeepers working the same Needs-you inbox is the ordinary case this row kind exists for. The loser sees an internal database error instead of 'somebody else answered first', which is exactly the benign cause the web module's own header predicts.
findings.required_fix: Take the row lock before the insert (a select ... for update on the extraction, or an advisory lock on the document) so the second caller re-reads the verdict and gets the existing no_parked_completeness_question refusal; or catch unique_violation and re-raise it as that refusal. Drive it with two connections in a cell.

findings.kind: false claim / drift risk on a shared file this lane owns alone
findings.title: BankTab in tree.ts is a hand-copy with no compile-time link to the bank workbench's own tab tuple
findings.where: apps/web/lib/navigation/tree.ts:138 (export type BankTab = "accounts" | ...) against apps/web/components/bank/bank-workbench.tsx:41-42 (const TABS = [...] as const; type BankTab = (typeof TABS)[number])
findings.evidence: bank-workbench.tsx imports nothing from @/lib/navigation/tree (its import list is next/navigation, next-intl, SectionTabs and its eight sections), and declares its own local TABS tuple and its own local BankTab. Renaming a view in that tuple would not red tree.ts. The ticket report's AC1 evidence claims the opposite: 'tab: "matching" is a BankTab literal (... the exact six values components/bank/bank-workbench.tsx's own TABS tuple accepts), so a rename of that view is a compile error here rather than a link that silently falls back.' No test cross-checks the two lists.
findings.why_it_matters: The claimed guarantee is the whole argument for typing the constant rather than spelling it inline, and it is not there. The two Needs-you rows this ticket repointed would silently fall back to the workbench's default if the view were ever renamed -- the exact failure the ticket exists to remove. RegisterTab has the same shape, so this is a house pattern rather than a new sin, but the claim made about it in the report is unverified.
findings.required_fix: Either export TABS from bank-workbench.tsx and derive tree.ts's BankTab from it (or the reverse), or add one cell asserting the two lists are equal. At minimum, correct the claim in the ticket report so the integrator does not carry it forward.

findings.title: tab: "matching" moves the bank destination for EVERY registry caller, and the workbench still defaults to accounts
findings.evidence: accountingHref is the only href builder, and it now appends ?tab=matching for the bank row. Its callers are components/app-shell/app-sidebar.tsx:433, components/accounting/accounting-hub.tsx:94, components/command/command-palette.tsx:239 and lib/command/routes.ts:276 (which is what builds CLIENT_ROUTES). bank-workbench.tsx:54 still reads const tab: BankTab = isTab(tabParam) ? tabParam : "accounts", and components/firm/client-home/client-bank-summary.tsx:107 still links to a bare /clients/:id/bank. The bank row's minimumRole is "viewer".
findings.why_it_matters: The ticket asked for two Needs-you rows to deep-link to Matching; what shipped also changes where the sidebar 'Bank' item, the accounting hub tile and the Cmd-K 'Bank' command land, for every member of every firm. A viewer now lands by default on the one bank view that is nothing but acts they cannot perform, while the client-home summary card and the workbench itself still treat Accounts as the bank's front door -- three surfaces, two answers.
findings.required_fix: Decide it explicitly rather than by side effect. Either keep the registry row bare and give the two Needs-you rows their ?tab=matching suffix directly (needs-you-links.ts already builds suffixes), or keep this and make the workbench's default and client-bank-summary.tsx agree. Say which in the report so the owner sees it as a product change.

findings.title: A viewer is offered the two buttons that post a payroll run
findings.evidence: clara.list_review_queue floors at clara.role_rank('viewer') (live body). Driven: carol, a viewer in firm A, reads the queue and sees 1 payroll_completeness_question row for the parked document. The affordance renders 'Yes -- this is everyone' / 'No -- lines are missing' unconditionally; pressing either is refused CLR04 'insufficient role' (driven).
findings.why_it_matters: Every other inline affordance behaves this way, so this is the house pattern and not a wall that is missing. It is worth one line anyway because this is the first inline affordance in the inbox that BOOKS A JOURNAL ENTRY, and 'Yes -- this is everyone' offered to somebody who cannot post reads as an invitation rather than as information.
findings.required_fix: None required for this lane. If the house pattern is ever revisited, this is the row to start with: render the question and the figures for a viewer and withhold the two buttons.

findings.kind: wrong reason on a safe outcome
findings.title: A printed page count of zero is reported as 'the summary names more pages than the one read'
findings.where: packages/db/migrations/0343_payroll_completeness_witness.sql:634-636 (the else arm of the page-count branch)
findings.evidence: Driven against clara.evaluate_payroll_run_state_v2: both channels answering payroll.run.page_count = '0' gives completeness {verdict: absent, reason: the_summary_names_more_pages_than_the_one_read}. The count regex ^[0-9]{1,6}$ admits 0.
findings.why_it_matters: The outcome is safe (absent -> the question is parked), and the reason never reaches a person directly -- the parked sentence is shown instead. It only appears in the verdict's detail, which is where the next reader will look when this lane misbehaves.
findings.required_fix: Admit 1..999999 rather than 0..999999 for a page count, or give a zero its own reason. Cosmetic.

findings.title: A mis-clicked 'no' is final for that reading, and the sentence tells the person to do the wrong thing
findings.evidence: Driven: after a 'no', a FRESH op key answering 'yes' on the same document is refused CLR10, detail {"reason":"no_parked_completeness_question"} -- the verdict now says completeness_declined and parked=false. The sentence a person then reads is 'Payroll run ... was not posted: <name> answered that this summary is not every employee for the month. Re-file a complete copy of the summary.' clara.request_reextraction (0025/0026) exists, so a re-read is reachable.
findings.why_it_matters: The model is deliberate and the migration argues it well ('a changed mind is a new reading'). But the instruction on screen assumes the answer was right and the DOCUMENT was wrong. For the ordinary case -- the person clicked the wrong button -- 're-file a complete copy' is the wrong remedy, and nothing on the row points at the re-read that would actually clear it.
findings.required_fix: Add the other half to the declined sentence: 'If that was a mistake, ask Clara to read the payslip again and the question is asked afresh.' No schema change.

not_defects_but_worth_the_integrator_kno: The page-count-of-one witness admits an UNATTENDED post on a basis the migration's own header calls insufficient ('it witnesses that the DOCUMENT is not truncated, not that the RUN is complete -- which is precisely the gap the row sum opens', 0343:47-49). A reading that misses a faint line in the middle of a single page satisfies it. The brief names this witness explicitly, so it is in scope and not a finding -- but it is the weakest thing in the lane and it posts with no human in the loop. Worth the owner's eyes before payrollFacts_v2 makes it reachable.

A parked payroll summary produces TWO Needs-you rows: payroll_completeness_question and the ordinary uncoded_filing (driven). SectionJ's argument that one document never produces two rows is about the payroll pair specifically and holds; the uncoded_filing coexistence is 0297 section H's own recorded model and predates this lane.

clara.list_review_queue now evaluates clara._payroll_posting_verdict TWICE per payroll filing per queue read (once in payroll_rows, once in payroll_witness_rows), and each evaluation calls clara._payroll_entry_plan and reads clara.coa_accounts. Not measured here; worth a look once a firm accumulates payroll summaries.

clara._payroll_completeness_answer renders answered_at 'at time zone UTC' with a Z suffix while 69 other sites in packages/db/migrations use Asia/Kuala_Lumpur. It is an explicit instant, not a calendar day, so it is honest -- flagged only so nobody mistakes it for a house-convention break.
#1061's migration 0342 adds no rig-meta cohort by design (it mints no name) and no pins-corpus entry (it contains no dynamic SQL). Both postures match 0245/0246 and I could not fault them.
A status-report request did not arrive during this review.
